title: I Only Asked About the Fountain
subject: A man new to town goes to his first residents' association AGM only to ask why the square's fountain has been dry since 2016, raises his hand at the wrong moment, and walks home elected treasurer, carrying a biscuit tin with £41.17 in it.
caption: Vintage calypso, 1950s Trinidadian storytelling calypso with a gentle shuffle. Nylon-string acoustic guitar strumming a syncopated calypso rhythm, upright bass on a bouncing two-beat, clarinet answering each vocal line, muted trumpet riffs between verses, bongos and shak-shak maracas. Dry vintage studio sound, close mics, slight tape warmth. Male tenor, lilting storytelling melody with crisp diction, chorus singers answering the refrain. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 108 BPM, F major. Witty, sunny, mock-indignant. No electronic drums, no soca synths, no autotune, no rap, no electric guitar distortion, no modern pop production.
lyrics:
[Intro - nylon guitar, clarinet, bongos]

[Verse 1]
I moved to the street in the month of May
Went to the meeting to have my say
One little question, I thought it was fair
Why is the fountain dry in the square?

[Pre-Chorus]
The chairman said, any volunteer?
I raised my hand to scratch my ear

[Chorus]
I only asked about the fountain
Now I'm the treasurer, Lord have mercy
Forty-one pounds and seventeen pence
In a biscuit tin, I only asked about the fountain

[Verse 2]
They gave me the tin and they gave me the key
A ledger, a pencil and a cup of tea
Dry since twenty-sixteen, they say
And my forty-one pounds won't fix it today

[Pre-Chorus]
The chairman said, all in favour, aye
I said, I only came to ask why

[Chorus]
I only asked about the fountain
Now I'm the treasurer, who will help me
Forty-one pounds and seventeen pence
And a dry fountain, I only asked about the fountain

[Outro - clarinet, muted trumpet, shak-shak]
Only asked about the fountain
